title: Warn when slicer runs code from outside the discovered project

sections.heading: Why
sections.body: Installed as an editable console script, `slicer` runs a fixed `src` path. Run inside a git worktree, it operates on the worktree's `.slicer/` (found by discovery) but executes the *main* checkout's code, so changes made to the worktree's source are not exercised. In this project a `slicer check` in a worktree silently ran stale code and appeared to do nothing until `PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m slicer` was used. Nothing signals the mismatch.

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
1. When the running module's file is not under the discovered project root, a one-line stderr note names both paths and suggests `PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m slicer`.
2. When they match (ordinary use), nothing is printed.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body: In `main`, compare the package's location to the discovered project root; when the running code is not under the project (a worktree / editable-install mismatch), print a single stderr hint. Do not change stdout or exit codes, and keep it quiet for the common case. Consider an env var or flag to silence it.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body: The note appears only on a mismatch; stdout and exit codes are unchanged. The suite and `slicer check` pass.

sections.heading: Git
sections.body: One commit. Do not tag or push.
